# COR061 `multiple-allocations-with-stat`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

One `allocate`/`deallocate` with `stat=` handles several objects.

## Why

When the statement fails, `stat` does not say which object failed, and the others may or may not
have been allocated: the error handling cannot know what to clean up. Allocate one object per
statement when checking `stat`.

## Reported

```fortran
allocate(a(n), b(n), stat=ierr)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
allocate(a(n), stat=ierr)
...
allocate(b(n), stat=ierr)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR061] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR061` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C182` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
